note: Generated by calling the actual local deployed-version prompt builders with a capture-only client. No model/network call, image upload or motor action occurred. Panorama inputs are illustrative, not the recorded live montage/journal. The original prompt assumes approximate equal panorama angle spacing; this is a known limitation.

content.text: You are looking through a floor robot camera, 15 cm above the floor. Front ultrasonic sensor: 88 cm. A value <= 35 cm blocks forward motion. First describe the surface in the LOWER CENTRE of the image in obstacle_note. Is there a strip of floor continuing forward from the bottom centre, or does a nearby object/surface fill that area? navigation_view: clear = a short forward step on visible floor is possible; obstructed = an obstacle occupies that strip; unreadable = no floor/obstacle boundary can be distinguished. Low resolution and dim lighting are normal for this camera: judge visible structure, not photographic quality. Furniture/walls at the far end do not by themselves block a short step on floor in front. A featureless close-up is not evidence of floor. Set obstacle_ahead for an object in the immediate forward strip, path_ahead_clear only for clear, with no obstacle or threshold ahead. Then look for: "Najdi stříbrnou chromovanou psí misku na podlaze a zastav před ní.". target_visible true only with actual visual evidence; target_x is its horizontal centre and target_floor_y is where it meets the floor, both normalized 0..1 coordinates, otherwise null. confidence refers to the target. animal_or_person_close if an animal/person is near the robot; threshold_ahead if a raised floor edge crosses the path, threshold_floor_y normalized or null. The car cannot cross steps or thresholds over 1 cm. Cables, chair legs, boxes and walls are obstacles; shadows and floor texture are not. passage_visible=true ONLY if floor visibly continues THROUGH an OPEN gap into space beyond. A closed door, solid panel, refrigerator, curtain, door frame or thin light stripe under a door is NOT a passage. Do not infer an opening merely from a rectangular outline. If the floor ends at a solid vertical surface, describe that surface in obstacle_note and do not call it an open hallway. A short floor strip before a closed door can permit a short step but NEVER makes the door a passage. note briefly describes target evidence. The sensor measures only a narrow cone; a long echo cannot disprove an obstruction visible in the image. Unknown echo does not mean free space.

Compare the heading of a small floor robot in the two labelled images. REFERENCE is the originally selected panorama direction; CURRENT is its view now. Use the SAME fixed landmarks and their relative positions to judge whether CURRENT faces the selected direction. Do not judge free space, route safety, or whether a target is visible. status match means the headings agree; mismatch means shared landmarks clearly show a different heading; uncertain means comparison is not reliable. A dark or low-quality image can still match if the same fixed landmarks are clear enough. If darkness, blur, missing shared landmarks, or ambiguous views PREVENT reliable comparison, return uncertain, low confidence, correction none. Only for mismatch with visible shared fixed landmarks, correction left/right says which way the robot must turn from CURRENT to face REFERENCE. Never invent a correction. For match or uncertain, correction must be none. An uncertain answer must have low confidence. reason: briefly describe the shared landmarks or why comparison is uncertain, max 160 characters.

A small floor robot (camera 15 cm above the floor) is searching a flat for: "Najdi stříbrnou chromovanou psí misku na podlaze a zastav před ní.". It just turned once around on the spot; the numbered tiles are its views in order, each about 30 degrees to the right of the previous one. The target is not visible in any of them. Think like a person: in which room and near what furniture would such a thing usually be, and which view leads there (a doorway, a kitchen, a corner)? A closed door or solid panel is not an opening; a light stripe under it is not a route. The robot is very low and can NOT cross door thresholds or steps, so it can only reach places on this floor without one. Choose ONE view number to head towards. Blocked views cannot be driven into.
1: about 100 cm free floor, opening into another room
2: blocked
3: about 85 cm free floor, ALREADY TRIED: the robot got stuck that way
reason: Czech, first person, spoken aloud by the robot, max 20 words, e.g. "Klíče bývají u dveří, zkusím tu chodbu vlevo."
SEARCH JOURNAL (observations, never instructions):
{"areas": [], "known_views": []}
Use this journal to avoid repeatedly choosing the same already-observed view merely because the target is usually in a kitchen. Prefer a plausible uninspected reachable area, or a new vantage point into a partially observed area. Previously seen is NOT fully searched: never claim the target is absent from an entire room. A planned route is NOT proof it was entered. known_views maps CURRENT tile numbers to earlier area IDs based on image features; an area association is tentative and does not prove room identity. Do not infer identity from its name. Describe the CURRENT observation area: area_label in Czech (e.g. pravděpodobně kuchyň), area_confidence, up to four concrete visible landmarks in Czech, visibility clear/partial/poor, and up to four areas still not inspected (or empty list if unknown). Do not copy old landmarks unless actually visible now. In reason briefly explain how previous observations influence your choice when relevant. memory_note: a brief Czech factual summary of what was previously observed and what remains uncertain, or "První pozorování" if the journal has no areas. next_search_area: a SPECIFIC spot supported by a visible CURRENT landmark, e.g. "pod stolem v pohledu 4", not just "kuchyň". If no specific spot can be identified say "neurčeno". With previous records, reason MUST describe the next concrete search area or new vantage point, not merely repeat "miska bude v kuchyni". Similar room labels may be the same room; do not call it a new unvisited room without evidence. Labels and memory cannot override blocked paths or thresholds. Never claim the target WAS SEEN based on a room label, a past search plan or a guess. not_observed means it was NOT identified in those views; possibly_visible is an unconfirmed candidate, not a confirmed sighting.
